public_task_requirement: Please implement a website for The All-In Bourbon Bar to showcase its products and services. The website should have functionalities for displaying menus, introducing the membership-only private poker room, and showcasing events and promotions. Users should be able to browse the website, view menus, learn about the private poker room, view events and promotions, and make online reservations or purchases. Use peach puff for container backgrounds and indian red for component visuals.

task_summary.requirement_coverage: The site was intended to showcase The All-In Bourbon Bar with menu browsing, a members-only poker room, events/promotions, and online reservations or purchases, using peach puff container backgrounds and indian red component visuals. Verified coverage includes a visible menu section, a private poker room information section, and an events/promotions section with RSVP buttons. The main functional gap is the reservation/purchase flow: the evaluation agent could not reach a reservation form or confirmation after interacting with RSVP controls, so the online reservation/purchase requirement was not fully demonstrated.
verified_strengths: Menu content is present with item names, descriptions, and prices.
The members-only poker room section is implemented and reachable from navigation.
Events and promotions are displayed with visible RSVP buttons.
The requested peach puff and indian red color scheme was observed as applied in the rendered pages.
primary_functional_risks: The RSVP interaction did not produce a reservation form or confirmation within the interaction budget, so the reservation/purchase path may be incomplete or non-functional.
The implementation appears tab-based and may not expose all requested content simultaneously, which can make discovery of key sections dependent on navigation state.
The final evaluation indicates the page was only partially validated for the reservation objective, leaving the booking flow as the main unresolved risk.
primary_visual_observations: The screenshot-based review reported no obvious rendering errors.
The menu page was visible and legible, with item cards and prices clearly shown.
The appearance evaluator noted that the poker room and events content were not visible on the first screen shown in the screenshot used for appearance scoring.
The color requirements were judged to be met in the visible rendering.

appearance_reflection.observed_result: The navigation bar has exactly 3 tabs: "Menu", "Poker Room", and "Events & Promotions". The rendered content is controlled by `v-if`, so only one section is shown at a time: `MenuSection`, `PokerRoom`, or `EventsPromotions`. The reviewer's first-screen note says there was no visible information about the private poker room or clear links to events and promotions.
appearance_reflection.likely_cause_or_limitation: The code does include a Poker Room tab and an Events & Promotions tab, so the issue is that those sections are not visible on the first screen when the page opens on the menu tab. This is an appearance limitation about what must be shown up front, not a missing build feature.
appearance_reflection.preventative_action: Make the first screen show the private poker room information and the events/promotions entry points without requiring the user to switch tabs first. Verify that the initial view contains visible poker-room content and clear links or tabs for events and promotions.
appearance_reflection.verification: Load the page and check the first screen before any clicks: the poker room information and the events/promotions navigation must already be visible.
appearance_reflection.transfer_limits: Applies to tabbed or section-swapping landing pages for hospitality, dining, or membership sites that need key sections visible immediately.

reflections.observed_result: The layout uses a single-column page shell with `main { padding: 2rem; }` and grid cards that rely on `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(24ch, 1fr))`. The supplied stylesheet includes no responsive breakpoint for the app layout itself, and the reviewer said responsiveness to smaller screens was not evident in the screenshot.
reflections.likely_cause_or_limitation: The code has a grid that can wrap cards, but there is no explicit responsive rule for the overall page layout or navigation in the supplied styles. That supports the reviewer's concern that mobile responsiveness is not evident on the first screen.
reflections.preventative_action: Add responsive layout rules that change the page structure at smaller widths, and verify that the navigation and content reflow cleanly on a narrow screen. The rendered page should show a deliberate small-screen layout, not only a default desktop arrangement.
reflections.verification: Resize the browser to a narrow width and confirm that the main layout and navigation still fit and remain readable without relying on the default wide-screen arrangement.
reflections.transfer_limits: Applies to responsive landing pages and section-based sites that must adapt to mobile screens.
